newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Beobanka to buy French stake in Franco-Yugo bank.
newsitem.headline: Beobanka to buy French stake in Franco-Yugo bank.

text.p: Yugoslavia's Beobanka said it agreed to buy out the stake of two French banks in Banque Franco-Yougoslave, but Paris sources said on Tuesday the buy-out must get the final nod from the Bank of France.
The Paris-based Banque Franco-Yougoslave, with 540 million French francs ($105 million) in capital and reserves, is the biggest Yugoslav joint stock bank established abroad.

"Beobanka has agreed with Societe Generale and Banque Paribas to buy out $35 million worth of their capital, reserves and voting rights in the Banque Franco-Yougoslave," Beobanka said in a company newsletter.
The deal reportedly signed on November 15 in Paris made Beobanka "the most important founding member of the French-Yugoslav bank," the bank said.

Beobanka spokesman Zoran Pavlovic said the move "represents a turnaround in Beobanka's business policy and efforts to boost its European presence. The idea of European orientation was born during the years of sanctions."
Analysts said that with the departure of French banks, Banque Franco-Yougoslave would remain entirely owned by interests from former Yugoslavia.
Major shareholders are from Serbia, with part of the stake owned by Croatian and Bosnian interests.

"Societe Generale and Banque Paribas want to go out from Banque Franco-Yougoslave as a part of their strategy to leave joint banking ventures," a source close to Banque Franco-Yougoslave in Paris told Reuters.
Societe Generale and Banque Paribas each offered for sale 12.8 million French francs of their capital in Banque Franco-Yougoslave.
"Each of the banks hold 9.725 percent of capital, but together they have 33.49 percent of voting rights," said the source who asked not to be named.
Beobanka, Yugoslavia's largest bank, expressed interest in buying out 80 percent of the offered stake, while Beogradska banka wants to buy the remainder, the source said.
But any decision on the buy-out needs approval by the Bank of France.

"Bank of France will first look at Beobanka and Beogradska banka books and check the level of their indebtedness. Only then will a decision on the (legal) future of the Yugoslav-French joint bank be made," the source said.

The source could not confirm the estimated value of capital, reserves and voting rights calculated by Beobanka, but said it was perhaps an over-optimistic figure because French banks also had some debts.
-- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254 ($ = 5.153 French Francs)
